defs.def: to be on your feet; to be in a vertical position 站立；立；直立

ex.s: Not standing a chance against competitive applicants, I came out of the interview with an upset look.
ex.t: 面对竞争的申请者,我没有机会,我从面试中走出来时,表情很沮丧。

ex.s: Unfortunately, between us stood the barrier of language.
ex.t: 不幸的是，我们之间横亘着语言的障碍。

ex.t: 写一份动物档案：丹顶鹤是世界上最高的鹤之一，站立时约150厘米高。

ex.src: 2024浙江1月卷·第四部分 写作

ex.t: 它用后腿站起来，推着木栅栏的柱子。

defs.def: to put sth/sb in a vertical position somewhere 使直立；竖放；使站立
to be in a particular place 位于（某处）

ex.s: St David’s Hall is the award winning National Concert Hall of Wales standing at the very heart of Cardiff’s entertainment centre.
ex.t: St David's Hall是威尔士获奖的国家音乐厅，位于卡迪夫娱乐中心的核心地带。

defs.def: to be in a particular condition or situation 处于（某种状态或情形）
to be a particular height 不用于进行时
to be at a particular level, amount, height, etc. 达特定水平（或数量、高度等）
to be in a particular place, especially while waiting to go somewhere 停；停靠

ex.s: When the car’s owner John Anderson and his colleague Carol Lawrence returned to the car—which was itself worth £35, 000—in Glasgow city centre, they were    23    to find two policemen standing next to it.
ex.t: 当车主John Anderson和他的同事Carol Lawrence回到那辆本身价值35,000英镑、停在格拉斯哥市中心的车时，他们____23____发现两名警察站在车旁。

ex.s: I was standing by the car when a hummingbird flew to the center of our group and began hovering.
ex.t: 我站在车旁时，一只蜂鸟飞到我们这群人的中央，开始悬停。

defs.def: to remain still, without moving or being moved 停滞；不流动；放着不动
if an offer, a decision, etc. made earlier stands, it is still valid 保持有效；维持不变

ex.s: Through it all, she remained in good academic standing and graduated with honors.
ex.t: 在整个过程中她保持了良好的学术成绩并以优异成绩毕业。

defs.def: to be in a situation where you are likely to do sth 很可能做某事

ex.s: Standing up for someone who is being treated unfairly can feel uncomfortable.
ex.t: 为受到不公平对待的人挺身而出可能会让人感到不舒服。

ex.s: But something about quantum computing makes it especially prone to hype, Johnson suggests, perhaps because “‘quantum’ stands for something cool you shouldn’t be able to understand.” And that brings me back to Taylor, who suggested that I read his book Q for Quantum.
ex.t: 但量子计算的某些特点使其特别容易受到炒作的影响，Johnson暗示道，也许是因为"'量子'代表着你本不该理解的酷东西。"这让我回到了Taylor身边，他建议我读他的书《Q for Quantum》。

defs.def: to have a particular attitude or opinion about sth or towards sb （对某事）持某种态度，有某一观点，采取某种立场

ex.s: I   56   twelve shades of green from where I stand.
ex.t: 从我的立场上看,我只有56个12个绿荫

defs.def: 不用于进行时
（尤与 can 或 could 连用）经受，承受，经得起

ex.s: Do not stand near street lights or under power lines.
ex.t: 不要站在路灯下或电线下面。

to be a candidate in an election 做候选人；参选
to move to one side 站到一边；让开

ex.s: After spotting a   18    on the front seat inside a parked car with its window down, he stood guard in the rain for about two hours waiting for the    19    to return.
ex.t: 看到一辆停着的车车窗摇下、前座上有个___18___后，他在雨中守了约两小时，等___19___回来。

defs.def: to not get involved in sth 不参与；不介入；置身事外
to stop doing a job so sb else can do it 退居一旁；让位予他人；靠边
to move back from a place 往后站；退后
to be located away from sth 位于离 … 有一段距离的地方

ex.s: But for all its ancient buildings, Beijing is also a place ____43____ welcomes the fast-paced development of modern life, with 21st-century architectural ____44____ (wonder) standing side by side with historical buildings of the past.
ex.t: 但尽管有许多古建筑，北京也是一个____43____欢迎现代生活快节奏发展的地方，21世纪的建筑____44____（wonder）与过去的历史建筑比邻而立。

ex.s: Even soccer fans tend to have a seat each; gone are the days of thousands standing to watch the match.
ex.t: 就连足球迷也倾向于每人有一个座位；成千上万人站着观看比赛的日子一去不复返了。

ex.t: 两种场景都是把狗放在一块玻璃屏风的一侧，屏风上在与狗鼻子齐高的位置有一些小孔，而实验员站在另一侧。

defs.def: to think about a situation as if you are not involved in it 置身事外（来考虑）

defs.def: to be ready for action 做好随时行动的准备；做好准备

ex.s: “I was turning the page to get ready for the next page, but the draft wind from the turn caused the spare pages to fall off the stand,” Mr Titterton said, “Luckily I was able to catch them and put them back.”
ex.t: “我正翻页准备下一页，但翻页带起的气流把备用的谱子从谱架上吹掉了，”蒂特顿先生说，“幸好我接住了它们并放回去。”
